limitations: Case series of 21 patients; all patient facts come from Tables 1, 3, 4 and 5 and are keyed by the printed Pt number, so patient ids p1 to p21 equal Pt 1 to 21.

Table 4 evidence quotes include the whole patient-number row and analyte row because the cell for one patient is only identifiable by column position; values for other patients appear inside those quotes.
Table 4 caption says 15 patients but 17 patient columns are printed (and the Results text says 17 TMA-like cases); this count mismatch is recorded as arithmetic ambiguity, not a source conflict.
Table 5 prints rows for 18 patients (Pt 17, 20 and 21 are absent) although its caption says 21 patients; no outcome facts are recorded for the absent patients.

Results text says 8 discontinued, 5 substituted and 5 continued the TKI among 18 patients, while Table 5 shows 14 discontinuations and 5 substitutions; arithmetic mismatch kept as ambiguity, no per-patient value changed.

Cohort-level statements (medians, percentages, unlabeled counts such as pre-existing renal comorbidity, schistocyte-negative smears in five cases, prior anti-VEGF antibody exposure in four cases, twelve patients with prior anticancer therapy, one AKI patient, four deaths from cancer progression, causality grades certain and probable) are not assigned to individual patients because the text gives no patient labels.
Table 2 is a group-level summary; only its BTK row (n = 1) is kept, as review_only facts for the sole BTK patient.
Cases 5 and 19 in the causality sentence are matched to Pt 5 and Pt 19 by number only, kept review_only.
Peak U-Pro for Pt 11 differs between Tables 3 and 5 and is kept as two review_only source_conflict facts; TKI duration for Pt 3 and Pt 6 differs only by rounding between Tables 1 and 3.
Table 5 Tumor status has no printed time and is not equated with the Table 1 status at biopsy.

Figure 1 as plotted sums to 18 cases (VEGFR 11, PDGFR 4, HER 2, BTK 1) while the text and tables give 21 patients (VEGFR 12, PDGFR 5, HER 3, BTK 1); plotted values are chart estimates, not facts, and no patient fact is derived from them.

Supplement Table S1 (DOCX) is an aggregate evidence-level count table by TKI group and holds no patient-level data; it could not be extracted with the text-document tool because anydoc is not installed, so only the manifest row was reviewed from the raw DOCX text.
Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; the four images were inspected separately in the visual submission.

Figure 1 covers 2015 to 2024 while the study window runs to March 2025, which may explain why its bars total 18 rather than 21; the source does not say so, so the difference stays an unexplained limitation.

The Results sentence that 5 patients started immunosuppressive therapy for significant proteinuria and/or renal impairment, guided by immune complex deposition, names no patients; Table 5 shows IS therapy for five patients (Pt 2, 3, 5, 14, 15), but the indication is not assigned to them.
Supplement Table S1 is an aggregate causality evidence-level count table (certain, probable, possible by TKI group); no per-patient values are taken from it.

The case series lists this patient as having biopsy-proven TKI-associated renal injury, with edema present and change in hypertension absent at the time of renal biopsy. Concomitant medication is not available.

Table 4 evidence quotes include the whole patient-number row and analyte row because the cell for one patient is only identifiable by column position; values for other patients appear inside those quotes.
Table 4 caption says 15 patients but 17 patient columns are printed (and the Results text says 17 TMA-like cases); this count mismatch is recorded as arithmetic ambiguity, not a source conflict.
Table 5 prints rows for 18 patients (Pt 17, 20 and 21 are absent) although its caption says 21 patients; no outcome facts are recorded for the absent patients.

Results text says 8 discontinued, 5 substituted and 5 continued the TKI among 18 patients, while Table 5 shows 14 discontinuations and 5 substitutions; arithmetic mismatch kept as ambiguity, no per-patient value changed.

Cohort-level statements (medians, percentages, unlabeled counts such as pre-existing renal comorbidity, schistocyte-negative smears in five cases, prior anti-VEGF antibody exposure in four cases, twelve patients with prior anticancer therapy, one AKI patient, four deaths from cancer progression, causality grades certain and probable) are not assigned to individual patients because the text gives no patient labels.
Table 2 is a group-level summary; only its BTK row (n = 1) is kept, as review_only facts for the sole BTK patient.
Cases 5 and 19 in the causality sentence are matched to Pt 5 and Pt 19 by number only, kept review_only.
Peak U-Pro for Pt 11 differs between Tables 3 and 5 and is kept as two review_only source_conflict facts; TKI duration for Pt 3 and Pt 6 differs only by rounding between Tables 1 and 3.
Table 5 Tumor status has no printed time and is not equated with the Table 1 status at biopsy.

Figure 1 as plotted sums to 18 cases (VEGFR 11, PDGFR 4, HER 2, BTK 1) while the text and tables give 21 patients (VEGFR 12, PDGFR 5, HER 3, BTK 1); plotted values are chart estimates, not facts, and no patient fact is derived from them.

Supplement Table S1 (DOCX) is an aggregate evidence-level count table by TKI group and holds no patient-level data; it could not be extracted with the text-document tool because anydoc is not installed, so only the manifest row was reviewed from the raw DOCX text.
Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; the four images were inspected separately in the visual submission.

Figure 1 covers 2015 to 2024 while the study window runs to March 2025, which may explain why its bars total 18 rather than 21; the source does not say so, so the difference stays an unexplained limitation.

The Results sentence that 5 patients started immunosuppressive therapy for significant proteinuria and/or renal impairment, guided by immune complex deposition, names no patients; Table 5 shows IS therapy for five patients (Pt 2, 3, 5, 14, 15), but the indication is not assigned to them.
Supplement Table S1 is an aggregate causality evidence-level count table (certain, probable, possible by TKI group); no per-patient values are taken from it.

limitations: Case series of 21 patients; all patient facts come from Tables 1, 3, 4 and 5 and are keyed by the printed Pt number, so patient ids p1 to p21 equal Pt 1 to 21.

Table 4 evidence quotes include the whole patient-number row and analyte row because the cell for one patient is only identifiable by column position; values for other patients appear inside those quotes.
Table 4 caption says 15 patients but 17 patient columns are printed (and the Results text says 17 TMA-like cases); this count mismatch is recorded as arithmetic ambiguity, not a source conflict.
Table 5 prints rows for 18 patients (Pt 17, 20 and 21 are absent) although its caption says 21 patients; no outcome facts are recorded for the absent patients.

Results text says 8 discontinued, 5 substituted and 5 continued the TKI among 18 patients, while Table 5 shows 14 discontinuations and 5 substitutions; arithmetic mismatch kept as ambiguity, no per-patient value changed.

Cohort-level statements (medians, percentages, unlabeled counts such as pre-existing renal comorbidity, schistocyte-negative smears in five cases, prior anti-VEGF antibody exposure in four cases, twelve patients with prior anticancer therapy, one AKI patient, four deaths from cancer progression, causality grades certain and probable) are not assigned to individual patients because the text gives no patient labels.
Table 2 is a group-level summary; only its BTK row (n = 1) is kept, as review_only facts for the sole BTK patient.
Cases 5 and 19 in the causality sentence are matched to Pt 5 and Pt 19 by number only, kept review_only.
Peak U-Pro for Pt 11 differs between Tables 3 and 5 and is kept as two review_only source_conflict facts; TKI duration for Pt 3 and Pt 6 differs only by rounding between Tables 1 and 3.
Table 5 Tumor status has no printed time and is not equated with the Table 1 status at biopsy.

Figure 1 as plotted sums to 18 cases (VEGFR 11, PDGFR 4, HER 2, BTK 1) while the text and tables give 21 patients (VEGFR 12, PDGFR 5, HER 3, BTK 1); plotted values are chart estimates, not facts, and no patient fact is derived from them.

Supplement Table S1 (DOCX) is an aggregate evidence-level count table by TKI group and holds no patient-level data; it could not be extracted with the text-document tool because anydoc is not installed, so only the manifest row was reviewed from the raw DOCX text.
Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; the four images were inspected separately in the visual submission.

Figure 1 covers 2015 to 2024 while the study window runs to March 2025, which may explain why its bars total 18 rather than 21; the source does not say so, so the difference stays an unexplained limitation.

The Results sentence that 5 patients started immunosuppressive therapy for significant proteinuria and/or renal impairment, guided by immune complex deposition, names no patients; Table 5 shows IS therapy for five patients (Pt 2, 3, 5, 14, 15), but the indication is not assigned to them.
Supplement Table S1 is an aggregate causality evidence-level count table (certain, probable, possible by TKI group); no per-patient values are taken from it.

limitations: Case series of 21 patients; all patient facts come from Tables 1, 3, 4 and 5 and are keyed by the printed Pt number, so patient ids p1 to p21 equal Pt 1 to 21.

Table 4 evidence quotes include the whole patient-number row and analyte row because the cell for one patient is only identifiable by column position; values for other patients appear inside those quotes.
Table 4 caption says 15 patients but 17 patient columns are printed (and the Results text says 17 TMA-like cases); this count mismatch is recorded as arithmetic ambiguity, not a source conflict.
Table 5 prints rows for 18 patients (Pt 17, 20 and 21 are absent) although its caption says 21 patients; no outcome facts are recorded for the absent patients.

Results text says 8 discontinued, 5 substituted and 5 continued the TKI among 18 patients, while Table 5 shows 14 discontinuations and 5 substitutions; arithmetic mismatch kept as ambiguity, no per-patient value changed.

Cohort-level statements (medians, percentages, unlabeled counts such as pre-existing renal comorbidity, schistocyte-negative smears in five cases, prior anti-VEGF antibody exposure in four cases, twelve patients with prior anticancer therapy, one AKI patient, four deaths from cancer progression, causality grades certain and probable) are not assigned to individual patients because the text gives no patient labels.
Table 2 is a group-level summary; only its BTK row (n = 1) is kept, as review_only facts for the sole BTK patient.
Cases 5 and 19 in the causality sentence are matched to Pt 5 and Pt 19 by number only, kept review_only.
Peak U-Pro for Pt 11 differs between Tables 3 and 5 and is kept as two review_only source_conflict facts; TKI duration for Pt 3 and Pt 6 differs only by rounding between Tables 1 and 3.
Table 5 Tumor status has no printed time and is not equated with the Table 1 status at biopsy.

Figure 1 as plotted sums to 18 cases (VEGFR 11, PDGFR 4, HER 2, BTK 1) while the text and tables give 21 patients (VEGFR 12, PDGFR 5, HER 3, BTK 1); plotted values are chart estimates, not facts, and no patient fact is derived from them.

Supplement Table S1 (DOCX) is an aggregate evidence-level count table by TKI group and holds no patient-level data; it could not be extracted with the text-document tool because anydoc is not installed, so only the manifest row was reviewed from the raw DOCX text.
Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; the four images were inspected separately in the visual submission.

Figure 1 covers 2015 to 2024 while the study window runs to March 2025, which may explain why its bars total 18 rather than 21; the source does not say so, so the difference stays an unexplained limitation.

The Results sentence that 5 patients started immunosuppressive therapy for significant proteinuria and/or renal impairment, guided by immune complex deposition, names no patients; Table 5 shows IS therapy for five patients (Pt 2, 3, 5, 14, 15), but the indication is not assigned to them.
Supplement Table S1 is an aggregate causality evidence-level count table (certain, probable, possible by TKI group); no per-patient values are taken from it.

limitations: Case series of 21 patients; all patient facts come from Tables 1, 3, 4 and 5 and are keyed by the printed Pt number, so patient ids p1 to p21 equal Pt 1 to 21.

Table 4 evidence quotes include the whole patient-number row and analyte row because the cell for one patient is only identifiable by column position; values for other patients appear inside those quotes.
Table 4 caption says 15 patients but 17 patient columns are printed (and the Results text says 17 TMA-like cases); this count mismatch is recorded as arithmetic ambiguity, not a source conflict.
Table 5 prints rows for 18 patients (Pt 17, 20 and 21 are absent) although its caption says 21 patients; no outcome facts are recorded for the absent patients.

Results text says 8 discontinued, 5 substituted and 5 continued the TKI among 18 patients, while Table 5 shows 14 discontinuations and 5 substitutions; arithmetic mismatch kept as ambiguity, no per-patient value changed.

Cohort-level statements (medians, percentages, unlabeled counts such as pre-existing renal comorbidity, schistocyte-negative smears in five cases, prior anti-VEGF antibody exposure in four cases, twelve patients with prior anticancer therapy, one AKI patient, four deaths from cancer progression, causality grades certain and probable) are not assigned to individual patients because the text gives no patient labels.
Table 2 is a group-level summary; only its BTK row (n = 1) is kept, as review_only facts for the sole BTK patient.
Cases 5 and 19 in the causality sentence are matched to Pt 5 and Pt 19 by number only, kept review_only.
Peak U-Pro for Pt 11 differs between Tables 3 and 5 and is kept as two review_only source_conflict facts; TKI duration for Pt 3 and Pt 6 differs only by rounding between Tables 1 and 3.
Table 5 Tumor status has no printed time and is not equated with the Table 1 status at biopsy.

Figure 1 as plotted sums to 18 cases (VEGFR 11, PDGFR 4, HER 2, BTK 1) while the text and tables give 21 patients (VEGFR 12, PDGFR 5, HER 3, BTK 1); plotted values are chart estimates, not facts, and no patient fact is derived from them.

Supplement Table S1 (DOCX) is an aggregate evidence-level count table by TKI group and holds no patient-level data; it could not be extracted with the text-document tool because anydoc is not installed, so only the manifest row was reviewed from the raw DOCX text.
Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; the four images were inspected separately in the visual submission.

Figure 1 covers 2015 to 2024 while the study window runs to March 2025, which may explain why its bars total 18 rather than 21; the source does not say so, so the difference stays an unexplained limitation.

The Results sentence that 5 patients started immunosuppressive therapy for significant proteinuria and/or renal impairment, guided by immune complex deposition, names no patients; Table 5 shows IS therapy for five patients (Pt 2, 3, 5, 14, 15), but the indication is not assigned to them.
Supplement Table S1 is an aggregate causality evidence-level count table (certain, probable, possible by TKI group); no per-patient values are taken from it.

Concomitant medication is listed as Pemetrexed, PTX, Platinum-based drugs.

limitations: Case series of 21 patients; all patient facts come from Tables 1, 3, 4 and 5 and are keyed by the printed Pt number, so patient ids p1 to p21 equal Pt 1 to 21.

Table 4 evidence quotes include the whole patient-number row and analyte row because the cell for one patient is only identifiable by column position; values for other patients appear inside those quotes.
Table 4 caption says 15 patients but 17 patient columns are printed (and the Results text says 17 TMA-like cases); this count mismatch is recorded as arithmetic ambiguity, not a source conflict.
Table 5 prints rows for 18 patients (Pt 17, 20 and 21 are absent) although its caption says 21 patients; no outcome facts are recorded for the absent patients.

Results text says 8 discontinued, 5 substituted and 5 continued the TKI among 18 patients, while Table 5 shows 14 discontinuations and 5 substitutions; arithmetic mismatch kept as ambiguity, no per-patient value changed.

Cohort-level statements (medians, percentages, unlabeled counts such as pre-existing renal comorbidity, schistocyte-negative smears in five cases, prior anti-VEGF antibody exposure in four cases, twelve patients with prior anticancer therapy, one AKI patient, four deaths from cancer progression, causality grades certain and probable) are not assigned to individual patients because the text gives no patient labels.
Table 2 is a group-level summary; only its BTK row (n = 1) is kept, as review_only facts for the sole BTK patient.
Cases 5 and 19 in the causality sentence are matched to Pt 5 and Pt 19 by number only, kept review_only.
Peak U-Pro for Pt 11 differs between Tables 3 and 5 and is kept as two review_only source_conflict facts; TKI duration for Pt 3 and Pt 6 differs only by rounding between Tables 1 and 3.
Table 5 Tumor status has no printed time and is not equated with the Table 1 status at biopsy.

Figure 1 as plotted sums to 18 cases (VEGFR 11, PDGFR 4, HER 2, BTK 1) while the text and tables give 21 patients (VEGFR 12, PDGFR 5, HER 3, BTK 1); plotted values are chart estimates, not facts, and no patient fact is derived from them.

Supplement Table S1 (DOCX) is an aggregate evidence-level count table by TKI group and holds no patient-level data; it could not be extracted with the text-document tool because anydoc is not installed, so only the manifest row was reviewed from the raw DOCX text.
Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; the four images were inspected separately in the visual submission.

Figure 1 covers 2015 to 2024 while the study window runs to March 2025, which may explain why its bars total 18 rather than 21; the source does not say so, so the difference stays an unexplained limitation.

The Results sentence that 5 patients started immunosuppressive therapy for significant proteinuria and/or renal impairment, guided by immune complex deposition, names no patients; Table 5 shows IS therapy for five patients (Pt 2, 3, 5, 14, 15), but the indication is not assigned to them.
Supplement Table S1 is an aggregate causality evidence-level count table (certain, probable, possible by TKI group); no per-patient values are taken from it.

claims.text: A female patient aged 50 years with thyroid cancer had received the tyrosine kinase inhibitor Lenvatinib for 53.4 months. The case series lists this patient as having biopsy-proven TKI-associated renal injury, with edema present and change in hypertension present at the time of renal biopsy. Concomitant medication is not available.

limitations: Case series of 21 patients; all patient facts come from Tables 1, 3, 4 and 5 and are keyed by the printed Pt number, so patient ids p1 to p21 equal Pt 1 to 21.

Table 4 evidence quotes include the whole patient-number row and analyte row because the cell for one patient is only identifiable by column position; values for other patients appear inside those quotes.
Table 4 caption says 15 patients but 17 patient columns are printed (and the Results text says 17 TMA-like cases); this count mismatch is recorded as arithmetic ambiguity, not a source conflict.
Table 5 prints rows for 18 patients (Pt 17, 20 and 21 are absent) although its caption says 21 patients; no outcome facts are recorded for the absent patients.

Results text says 8 discontinued, 5 substituted and 5 continued the TKI among 18 patients, while Table 5 shows 14 discontinuations and 5 substitutions; arithmetic mismatch kept as ambiguity, no per-patient value changed.

Cohort-level statements (medians, percentages, unlabeled counts such as pre-existing renal comorbidity, schistocyte-negative smears in five cases, prior anti-VEGF antibody exposure in four cases, twelve patients with prior anticancer therapy, one AKI patient, four deaths from cancer progression, causality grades certain and probable) are not assigned to individual patients because the text gives no patient labels.
Table 2 is a group-level summary; only its BTK row (n = 1) is kept, as review_only facts for the sole BTK patient.
Cases 5 and 19 in the causality sentence are matched to Pt 5 and Pt 19 by number only, kept review_only.
Peak U-Pro for Pt 11 differs between Tables 3 and 5 and is kept as two review_only source_conflict facts; TKI duration for Pt 3 and Pt 6 differs only by rounding between Tables 1 and 3.
Table 5 Tumor status has no printed time and is not equated with the Table 1 status at biopsy.

Figure 1 as plotted sums to 18 cases (VEGFR 11, PDGFR 4, HER 2, BTK 1) while the text and tables give 21 patients (VEGFR 12, PDGFR 5, HER 3, BTK 1); plotted values are chart estimates, not facts, and no patient fact is derived from them.

Supplement Table S1 (DOCX) is an aggregate evidence-level count table by TKI group and holds no patient-level data; it could not be extracted with the text-document tool because anydoc is not installed, so only the manifest row was reviewed from the raw DOCX text.
Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; the four images were inspected separately in the visual submission.

Figure 1 covers 2015 to 2024 while the study window runs to March 2025, which may explain why its bars total 18 rather than 21; the source does not say so, so the difference stays an unexplained limitation.

The Results sentence that 5 patients started immunosuppressive therapy for significant proteinuria and/or renal impairment, guided by immune complex deposition, names no patients; Table 5 shows IS therapy for five patients (Pt 2, 3, 5, 14, 15), but the indication is not assigned to them.
Supplement Table S1 is an aggregate causality evidence-level count table (certain, probable, possible by TKI group); no per-patient values are taken from it.

The case series lists this patient as having biopsy-proven TKI-associated renal injury, with edema present and change in hypertension absent at the time of renal biopsy. Concomitant medication is not available.

limitations: Case series of 21 patients; all patient facts come from Tables 1, 3, 4 and 5 and are keyed by the printed Pt number, so patient ids p1 to p21 equal Pt 1 to 21.

Table 4 evidence quotes include the whole patient-number row and analyte row because the cell for one patient is only identifiable by column position; values for other patients appear inside those quotes.
Table 4 caption says 15 patients but 17 patient columns are printed (and the Results text says 17 TMA-like cases); this count mismatch is recorded as arithmetic ambiguity, not a source conflict.
Table 5 prints rows for 18 patients (Pt 17, 20 and 21 are absent) although its caption says 21 patients; no outcome facts are recorded for the absent patients.

Results text says 8 discontinued, 5 substituted and 5 continued the TKI among 18 patients, while Table 5 shows 14 discontinuations and 5 substitutions; arithmetic mismatch kept as ambiguity, no per-patient value changed.

Cohort-level statements (medians, percentages, unlabeled counts such as pre-existing renal comorbidity, schistocyte-negative smears in five cases, prior anti-VEGF antibody exposure in four cases, twelve patients with prior anticancer therapy, one AKI patient, four deaths from cancer progression, causality grades certain and probable) are not assigned to individual patients because the text gives no patient labels.
Table 2 is a group-level summary; only its BTK row (n = 1) is kept, as review_only facts for the sole BTK patient.
Cases 5 and 19 in the causality sentence are matched to Pt 5 and Pt 19 by number only, kept review_only.
Peak U-Pro for Pt 11 differs between Tables 3 and 5 and is kept as two review_only source_conflict facts; TKI duration for Pt 3 and Pt 6 differs only by rounding between Tables 1 and 3.
Table 5 Tumor status has no printed time and is not equated with the Table 1 status at biopsy.

Figure 1 as plotted sums to 18 cases (VEGFR 11, PDGFR 4, HER 2, BTK 1) while the text and tables give 21 patients (VEGFR 12, PDGFR 5, HER 3, BTK 1); plotted values are chart estimates, not facts, and no patient fact is derived from them.

Supplement Table S1 (DOCX) is an aggregate evidence-level count table by TKI group and holds no patient-level data; it could not be extracted with the text-document tool because anydoc is not installed, so only the manifest row was reviewed from the raw DOCX text.
Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; the four images were inspected separately in the visual submission.

Figure 1 covers 2015 to 2024 while the study window runs to March 2025, which may explain why its bars total 18 rather than 21; the source does not say so, so the difference stays an unexplained limitation.

The Results sentence that 5 patients started immunosuppressive therapy for significant proteinuria and/or renal impairment, guided by immune complex deposition, names no patients; Table 5 shows IS therapy for five patients (Pt 2, 3, 5, 14, 15), but the indication is not assigned to them.
Supplement Table S1 is an aggregate causality evidence-level count table (certain, probable, possible by TKI group); no per-patient values are taken from it.

claims.text: A male patient aged 54 years with stomach cancer had received the tyrosine kinase inhibitor Apatinib for 53 months. The case series lists this patient as having biopsy-proven TKI-associated renal injury, with edema present and change in hypertension present at the time of renal biopsy. Concomitant medication is not available.

limitations: Case series of 21 patients; all patient facts come from Tables 1, 3, 4 and 5 and are keyed by the printed Pt number, so patient ids p1 to p21 equal Pt 1 to 21.

Table 4 evidence quotes include the whole patient-number row and analyte row because the cell for one patient is only identifiable by column position; values for other patients appear inside those quotes.
Table 4 caption says 15 patients but 17 patient columns are printed (and the Results text says 17 TMA-like cases); this count mismatch is recorded as arithmetic ambiguity, not a source conflict.
Table 5 prints rows for 18 patients (Pt 17, 20 and 21 are absent) although its caption says 21 patients; no outcome facts are recorded for the absent patients.

Results text says 8 discontinued, 5 substituted and 5 continued the TKI among 18 patients, while Table 5 shows 14 discontinuations and 5 substitutions; arithmetic mismatch kept as ambiguity, no per-patient value changed.

Cohort-level statements (medians, percentages, unlabeled counts such as pre-existing renal comorbidity, schistocyte-negative smears in five cases, prior anti-VEGF antibody exposure in four cases, twelve patients with prior anticancer therapy, one AKI patient, four deaths from cancer progression, causality grades certain and probable) are not assigned to individual patients because the text gives no patient labels.
Table 2 is a group-level summary; only its BTK row (n = 1) is kept, as review_only facts for the sole BTK patient.
Cases 5 and 19 in the causality sentence are matched to Pt 5 and Pt 19 by number only, kept review_only.
Peak U-Pro for Pt 11 differs between Tables 3 and 5 and is kept as two review_only source_conflict facts; TKI duration for Pt 3 and Pt 6 differs only by rounding between Tables 1 and 3.
Table 5 Tumor status has no printed time and is not equated with the Table 1 status at biopsy.

Figure 1 as plotted sums to 18 cases (VEGFR 11, PDGFR 4, HER 2, BTK 1) while the text and tables give 21 patients (VEGFR 12, PDGFR 5, HER 3, BTK 1); plotted values are chart estimates, not facts, and no patient fact is derived from them.

Supplement Table S1 (DOCX) is an aggregate evidence-level count table by TKI group and holds no patient-level data; it could not be extracted with the text-document tool because anydoc is not installed, so only the manifest row was reviewed from the raw DOCX text.
Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; the four images were inspected separately in the visual submission.

Figure 1 covers 2015 to 2024 while the study window runs to March 2025, which may explain why its bars total 18 rather than 21; the source does not say so, so the difference stays an unexplained limitation.

The Results sentence that 5 patients started immunosuppressive therapy for significant proteinuria and/or renal impairment, guided by immune complex deposition, names no patients; Table 5 shows IS therapy for five patients (Pt 2, 3, 5, 14, 15), but the indication is not assigned to them.
Supplement Table S1 is an aggregate causality evidence-level count table (certain, probable, possible by TKI group); no per-patient values are taken from it.

Concomitant medication is not available.

limitations: Case series of 21 patients; all patient facts come from Tables 1, 3, 4 and 5 and are keyed by the printed Pt number, so patient ids p1 to p21 equal Pt 1 to 21.

Table 4 evidence quotes include the whole patient-number row and analyte row because the cell for one patient is only identifiable by column position; values for other patients appear inside those quotes.
Table 4 caption says 15 patients but 17 patient columns are printed (and the Results text says 17 TMA-like cases); this count mismatch is recorded as arithmetic ambiguity, not a source conflict.
Table 5 prints rows for 18 patients (Pt 17, 20 and 21 are absent) although its caption says 21 patients; no outcome facts are recorded for the absent patients.

Results text says 8 discontinued, 5 substituted and 5 continued the TKI among 18 patients, while Table 5 shows 14 discontinuations and 5 substitutions; arithmetic mismatch kept as ambiguity, no per-patient value changed.

Cohort-level statements (medians, percentages, unlabeled counts such as pre-existing renal comorbidity, schistocyte-negative smears in five cases, prior anti-VEGF antibody exposure in four cases, twelve patients with prior anticancer therapy, one AKI patient, four deaths from cancer progression, causality grades certain and probable) are not assigned to individual patients because the text gives no patient labels.
Table 2 is a group-level summary; only its BTK row (n = 1) is kept, as review_only facts for the sole BTK patient.
Cases 5 and 19 in the causality sentence are matched to Pt 5 and Pt 19 by number only, kept review_only.
Peak U-Pro for Pt 11 differs between Tables 3 and 5 and is kept as two review_only source_conflict facts; TKI duration for Pt 3 and Pt 6 differs only by rounding between Tables 1 and 3.
Table 5 Tumor status has no printed time and is not equated with the Table 1 status at biopsy.

Figure 1 as plotted sums to 18 cases (VEGFR 11, PDGFR 4, HER 2, BTK 1) while the text and tables give 21 patients (VEGFR 12, PDGFR 5, HER 3, BTK 1); plotted values are chart estimates, not facts, and no patient fact is derived from them.

Supplement Table S1 (DOCX) is an aggregate evidence-level count table by TKI group and holds no patient-level data; it could not be extracted with the text-document tool because anydoc is not installed, so only the manifest row was reviewed from the raw DOCX text.
Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; the four images were inspected separately in the visual submission.

Figure 1 covers 2015 to 2024 while the study window runs to March 2025, which may explain why its bars total 18 rather than 21; the source does not say so, so the difference stays an unexplained limitation.

The Results sentence that 5 patients started immunosuppressive therapy for significant proteinuria and/or renal impairment, guided by immune complex deposition, names no patients; Table 5 shows IS therapy for five patients (Pt 2, 3, 5, 14, 15), but the indication is not assigned to them.
Supplement Table S1 is an aggregate causality evidence-level count table (certain, probable, possible by TKI group); no per-patient values are taken from it.

claims.text: A male patient aged 59 years with gastrointestinal stromal tumor had received the tyrosine kinase inhibitor Sunitinib for 26 months. The case series lists this patient as having biopsy-proven TKI-associated renal injury, with edema absent and change in hypertension present at the time of renal biopsy. Concomitant medication is not available.

limitations: Case series of 21 patients; all patient facts come from Tables 1, 3, 4 and 5 and are keyed by the printed Pt number, so patient ids p1 to p21 equal Pt 1 to 21.

Table 4 evidence quotes include the whole patient-number row and analyte row because the cell for one patient is only identifiable by column position; values for other patients appear inside those quotes.
Table 4 caption says 15 patients but 17 patient columns are printed (and the Results text says 17 TMA-like cases); this count mismatch is recorded as arithmetic ambiguity, not a source conflict.
Table 5 prints rows for 18 patients (Pt 17, 20 and 21 are absent) although its caption says 21 patients; no outcome facts are recorded for the absent patients.

Results text says 8 discontinued, 5 substituted and 5 continued the TKI among 18 patients, while Table 5 shows 14 discontinuations and 5 substitutions; arithmetic mismatch kept as ambiguity, no per-patient value changed.

Cohort-level statements (medians, percentages, unlabeled counts such as pre-existing renal comorbidity, schistocyte-negative smears in five cases, prior anti-VEGF antibody exposure in four cases, twelve patients with prior anticancer therapy, one AKI patient, four deaths from cancer progression, causality grades certain and probable) are not assigned to individual patients because the text gives no patient labels.
Table 2 is a group-level summary; only its BTK row (n = 1) is kept, as review_only facts for the sole BTK patient.
Cases 5 and 19 in the causality sentence are matched to Pt 5 and Pt 19 by number only, kept review_only.
Peak U-Pro for Pt 11 differs between Tables 3 and 5 and is kept as two review_only source_conflict facts; TKI duration for Pt 3 and Pt 6 differs only by rounding between Tables 1 and 3.
Table 5 Tumor status has no printed time and is not equated with the Table 1 status at biopsy.

Figure 1 as plotted sums to 18 cases (VEGFR 11, PDGFR 4, HER 2, BTK 1) while the text and tables give 21 patients (VEGFR 12, PDGFR 5, HER 3, BTK 1); plotted values are chart estimates, not facts, and no patient fact is derived from them.

Supplement Table S1 (DOCX) is an aggregate evidence-level count table by TKI group and holds no patient-level data; it could not be extracted with the text-document tool because anydoc is not installed, so only the manifest row was reviewed from the raw DOCX text.
Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; the four images were inspected separately in the visual submission.

Figure 1 covers 2015 to 2024 while the study window runs to March 2025, which may explain why its bars total 18 rather than 21; the source does not say so, so the difference stays an unexplained limitation.

The Results sentence that 5 patients started immunosuppressive therapy for significant proteinuria and/or renal impairment, guided by immune complex deposition, names no patients; Table 5 shows IS therapy for five patients (Pt 2, 3, 5, 14, 15), but the indication is not assigned to them.
Supplement Table S1 is an aggregate causality evidence-level count table (certain, probable, possible by TKI group); no per-patient values are taken from it.

claims.text: A female patient aged 60 years with chronic myeloid leukemia had received the tyrosine kinase inhibitor Dasatinib for 59 months. The case series lists this patient as having biopsy-proven TKI-associated renal injury, with edema absent and change in hypertension absent at the time of renal biopsy. Concomitant medication is not available.

limitations: Case series of 21 patients; all patient facts come from Tables 1, 3, 4 and 5 and are keyed by the printed Pt number, so patient ids p1 to p21 equal Pt 1 to 21.

Table 4 evidence quotes include the whole patient-number row and analyte row because the cell for one patient is only identifiable by column position; values for other patients appear inside those quotes.
Table 4 caption says 15 patients but 17 patient columns are printed (and the Results text says 17 TMA-like cases); this count mismatch is recorded as arithmetic ambiguity, not a source conflict.
Table 5 prints rows for 18 patients (Pt 17, 20 and 21 are absent) although its caption says 21 patients; no outcome facts are recorded for the absent patients.

Results text says 8 discontinued, 5 substituted and 5 continued the TKI among 18 patients, while Table 5 shows 14 discontinuations and 5 substitutions; arithmetic mismatch kept as ambiguity, no per-patient value changed.

Cohort-level statements (medians, percentages, unlabeled counts such as pre-existing renal comorbidity, schistocyte-negative smears in five cases, prior anti-VEGF antibody exposure in four cases, twelve patients with prior anticancer therapy, one AKI patient, four deaths from cancer progression, causality grades certain and probable) are not assigned to individual patients because the text gives no patient labels.
Table 2 is a group-level summary; only its BTK row (n = 1) is kept, as review_only facts for the sole BTK patient.
Cases 5 and 19 in the causality sentence are matched to Pt 5 and Pt 19 by number only, kept review_only.
Peak U-Pro for Pt 11 differs between Tables 3 and 5 and is kept as two review_only source_conflict facts; TKI duration for Pt 3 and Pt 6 differs only by rounding between Tables 1 and 3.
Table 5 Tumor status has no printed time and is not equated with the Table 1 status at biopsy.

Figure 1 as plotted sums to 18 cases (VEGFR 11, PDGFR 4, HER 2, BTK 1) while the text and tables give 21 patients (VEGFR 12, PDGFR 5, HER 3, BTK 1); plotted values are chart estimates, not facts, and no patient fact is derived from them.

Supplement Table S1 (DOCX) is an aggregate evidence-level count table by TKI group and holds no patient-level data; it could not be extracted with the text-document tool because anydoc is not installed, so only the manifest row was reviewed from the raw DOCX text.
Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; the four images were inspected separately in the visual submission.

Figure 1 covers 2015 to 2024 while the study window runs to March 2025, which may explain why its bars total 18 rather than 21; the source does not say so, so the difference stays an unexplained limitation.

The Results sentence that 5 patients started immunosuppressive therapy for significant proteinuria and/or renal impairment, guided by immune complex deposition, names no patients; Table 5 shows IS therapy for five patients (Pt 2, 3, 5, 14, 15), but the indication is not assigned to them.
Supplement Table S1 is an aggregate causality evidence-level count table (certain, probable, possible by TKI group); no per-patient values are taken from it.

claims.text: A female patient aged 59 years with breast cancer had received the tyrosine kinase inhibitor Pyrotinib for 34 months. The case series lists this patient as having biopsy-proven TKI-associated renal injury, with edema absent and change in hypertension absent at the time of renal biopsy. Concomitant medication is not available.

limitations: Case series of 21 patients; all patient facts come from Tables 1, 3, 4 and 5 and are keyed by the printed Pt number, so patient ids p1 to p21 equal Pt 1 to 21.

Table 4 evidence quotes include the whole patient-number row and analyte row because the cell for one patient is only identifiable by column position; values for other patients appear inside those quotes.
Table 4 caption says 15 patients but 17 patient columns are printed (and the Results text says 17 TMA-like cases); this count mismatch is recorded as arithmetic ambiguity, not a source conflict.
Table 5 prints rows for 18 patients (Pt 17, 20 and 21 are absent) although its caption says 21 patients; no outcome facts are recorded for the absent patients.

Results text says 8 discontinued, 5 substituted and 5 continued the TKI among 18 patients, while Table 5 shows 14 discontinuations and 5 substitutions; arithmetic mismatch kept as ambiguity, no per-patient value changed.

Cohort-level statements (medians, percentages, unlabeled counts such as pre-existing renal comorbidity, schistocyte-negative smears in five cases, prior anti-VEGF antibody exposure in four cases, twelve patients with prior anticancer therapy, one AKI patient, four deaths from cancer progression, causality grades certain and probable) are not assigned to individual patients because the text gives no patient labels.
Table 2 is a group-level summary; only its BTK row (n = 1) is kept, as review_only facts for the sole BTK patient.
Cases 5 and 19 in the causality sentence are matched to Pt 5 and Pt 19 by number only, kept review_only.
Peak U-Pro for Pt 11 differs between Tables 3 and 5 and is kept as two review_only source_conflict facts; TKI duration for Pt 3 and Pt 6 differs only by rounding between Tables 1 and 3.
Table 5 Tumor status has no printed time and is not equated with the Table 1 status at biopsy.

Figure 1 as plotted sums to 18 cases (VEGFR 11, PDGFR 4, HER 2, BTK 1) while the text and tables give 21 patients (VEGFR 12, PDGFR 5, HER 3, BTK 1); plotted values are chart estimates, not facts, and no patient fact is derived from them.

Supplement Table S1 (DOCX) is an aggregate evidence-level count table by TKI group and holds no patient-level data; it could not be extracted with the text-document tool because anydoc is not installed, so only the manifest row was reviewed from the raw DOCX text.
Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; the four images were inspected separately in the visual submission.

Figure 1 covers 2015 to 2024 while the study window runs to March 2025, which may explain why its bars total 18 rather than 21; the source does not say so, so the difference stays an unexplained limitation.

The Results sentence that 5 patients started immunosuppressive therapy for significant proteinuria and/or renal impairment, guided by immune complex deposition, names no patients; Table 5 shows IS therapy for five patients (Pt 2, 3, 5, 14, 15), but the indication is not assigned to them.
Supplement Table S1 is an aggregate causality evidence-level count table (certain, probable, possible by TKI group); no per-patient values are taken from it.

limitations: Case series of 21 patients; all patient facts come from Tables 1, 3, 4 and 5 and are keyed by the printed Pt number, so patient ids p1 to p21 equal Pt 1 to 21.

Table 4 evidence quotes include the whole patient-number row and analyte row because the cell for one patient is only identifiable by column position; values for other patients appear inside those quotes.
Table 4 caption says 15 patients but 17 patient columns are printed (and the Results text says 17 TMA-like cases); this count mismatch is recorded as arithmetic ambiguity, not a source conflict.
Table 5 prints rows for 18 patients (Pt 17, 20 and 21 are absent) although its caption says 21 patients; no outcome facts are recorded for the absent patients.

Results text says 8 discontinued, 5 substituted and 5 continued the TKI among 18 patients, while Table 5 shows 14 discontinuations and 5 substitutions; arithmetic mismatch kept as ambiguity, no per-patient value changed.

Cohort-level statements (medians, percentages, unlabeled counts such as pre-existing renal comorbidity, schistocyte-negative smears in five cases, prior anti-VEGF antibody exposure in four cases, twelve patients with prior anticancer therapy, one AKI patient, four deaths from cancer progression, causality grades certain and probable) are not assigned to individual patients because the text gives no patient labels.
Table 2 is a group-level summary; only its BTK row (n = 1) is kept, as review_only facts for the sole BTK patient.
Cases 5 and 19 in the causality sentence are matched to Pt 5 and Pt 19 by number only, kept review_only.
Peak U-Pro for Pt 11 differs between Tables 3 and 5 and is kept as two review_only source_conflict facts; TKI duration for Pt 3 and Pt 6 differs only by rounding between Tables 1 and 3.
Table 5 Tumor status has no printed time and is not equated with the Table 1 status at biopsy.

Figure 1 as plotted sums to 18 cases (VEGFR 11, PDGFR 4, HER 2, BTK 1) while the text and tables give 21 patients (VEGFR 12, PDGFR 5, HER 3, BTK 1); plotted values are chart estimates, not facts, and no patient fact is derived from them.

Supplement Table S1 (DOCX) is an aggregate evidence-level count table by TKI group and holds no patient-level data; it could not be extracted with the text-document tool because anydoc is not installed, so only the manifest row was reviewed from the raw DOCX text.
Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; the four images were inspected separately in the visual submission.

Figure 1 covers 2015 to 2024 while the study window runs to March 2025, which may explain why its bars total 18 rather than 21; the source does not say so, so the difference stays an unexplained limitation.

The Results sentence that 5 patients started immunosuppressive therapy for significant proteinuria and/or renal impairment, guided by immune complex deposition, names no patients; Table 5 shows IS therapy for five patients (Pt 2, 3, 5, 14, 15), but the indication is not assigned to them.
Supplement Table S1 is an aggregate causality evidence-level count table (certain, probable, possible by TKI group); no per-patient values are taken from it.

Peak U-Pro for Pt 11 differs between Tables 3 and 5 and is kept as two review_only source_conflict facts; TKI duration for Pt 3 and Pt 6 differs only by rounding between Tables 1 and 3.
Table 5 Tumor status has no printed time and is not equated with the Table 1 status at biopsy.

Figure 1 as plotted sums to 18 cases (VEGFR 11, PDGFR 4, HER 2, BTK 1) while the text and tables give 21 patients (VEGFR 12, PDGFR 5, HER 3, BTK 1); plotted values are chart estimates, not facts, and no patient fact is derived from them.

Supplement Table S1 (DOCX) is an aggregate evidence-level count table by TKI group and holds no patient-level data; it could not be extracted with the text-document tool because anydoc is not installed, so only the manifest row was reviewed from the raw DOCX text.
Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; the four images were inspected separately in the visual submission.

Figure 1 covers 2015 to 2024 while the study window runs to March 2025, which may explain why its bars total 18 rather than 21; the source does not say so, so the difference stays an unexplained limitation.

The Results sentence that 5 patients started immunosuppressive therapy for significant proteinuria and/or renal impairment, guided by immune complex deposition, names no patients; Table 5 shows IS therapy for five patients (Pt 2, 3, 5, 14, 15), but the indication is not assigned to them.
Supplement Table S1 is an aggregate causality evidence-level count table (certain, probable, possible by TKI group); no per-patient values are taken from it.

Table 2 is a group-level summary; only its BTK row (n = 1) is kept, as review_only facts for the sole BTK patient.

Peak U-Pro for Pt 11 differs between Tables 3 and 5 and is kept as two review_only source_conflict facts; TKI duration for Pt 3 and Pt 6 differs only by rounding between Tables 1 and 3.
Table 5 Tumor status has no printed time and is not equated with the Table 1 status at biopsy.

Figure 1 as plotted sums to 18 cases (VEGFR 11, PDGFR 4, HER 2, BTK 1) while the text and tables give 21 patients (VEGFR 12, PDGFR 5, HER 3, BTK 1); plotted values are chart estimates, not facts, and no patient fact is derived from them.

Supplement Table S1 (DOCX) is an aggregate evidence-level count table by TKI group and holds no patient-level data; it could not be extracted with the text-document tool because anydoc is not installed, so only the manifest row was reviewed from the raw DOCX text.
Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; the four images were inspected separately in the visual submission.

Figure 1 covers 2015 to 2024 while the study window runs to March 2025, which may explain why its bars total 18 rather than 21; the source does not say so, so the difference stays an unexplained limitation.

The Results sentence that 5 patients started immunosuppressive therapy for significant proteinuria and/or renal impairment, guided by immune complex deposition, names no patients; Table 5 shows IS therapy for five patients (Pt 2, 3, 5, 14, 15), but the indication is not assigned to them.
Supplement Table S1 is an aggregate causality evidence-level count table (certain, probable, possible by TKI group); no per-patient values are taken from it.

claims.text: A male patient aged 69 years with liver cancer had received the tyrosine kinase inhibitor Lenvatinib for 41 months. The case series lists this patient as having biopsy-proven TKI-associated renal injury, with edema present and change in hypertension present at the time of renal biopsy. Concomitant medication is listed as Tenofovir disoproxil.

claims.text: Renal biopsy findings were reported as TMA + FSGS. At the time of renal biopsy, the table gives serum creatinine 1.3 (111) mg/dL (micromole per liter in parentheses), proteinuria 3.44 g/day and serum albumin 32.5 g/L. Nephrotic syndrome is recorded as yes, and the creatinine trajectory group is not assessable.

limitations: Case series of 21 patients; all patient facts come from Tables 1, 3, 4 and 5 and are keyed by the printed Pt number, so patient ids p1 to p21 equal Pt 1 to 21.

Table 4 evidence quotes include the whole patient-number row and analyte row because the cell for one patient is only identifiable by column position; values for other patients appear inside those quotes.
Table 4 caption says 15 patients but 17 patient columns are printed (and the Results text says 17 TMA-like cases); this count mismatch is recorded as arithmetic ambiguity, not a source conflict.
Table 5 prints rows for 18 patients (Pt 17, 20 and 21 are absent) although its caption says 21 patients; no outcome facts are recorded for the absent patients.

Results text says 8 discontinued, 5 substituted and 5 continued the TKI among 18 patients, while Table 5 shows 14 discontinuations and 5 substitutions; arithmetic mismatch kept as ambiguity, no per-patient value changed.

Cohort-level statements (medians, percentages, unlabeled counts such as pre-existing renal comorbidity, schistocyte-negative smears in five cases, prior anti-VEGF antibody exposure in four cases, twelve patients with prior anticancer therapy, one AKI patient, four deaths from cancer progression, causality grades certain and probable) are not assigned to individual patients because the text gives no patient labels.
Table 2 is a group-level summary; only its BTK row (n = 1) is kept, as review_only facts for the sole BTK patient.
Cases 5 and 19 in the causality sentence are matched to Pt 5 and Pt 19 by number only, kept review_only.
Peak U-Pro for Pt 11 differs between Tables 3 and 5 and is kept as two review_only source_conflict facts; TKI duration for Pt 3 and Pt 6 differs only by rounding between Tables 1 and 3.
Table 5 Tumor status has no printed time and is not equated with the Table 1 status at biopsy.

Figure 1 as plotted sums to 18 cases (VEGFR 11, PDGFR 4, HER 2, BTK 1) while the text and tables give 21 patients (VEGFR 12, PDGFR 5, HER 3, BTK 1); plotted values are chart estimates, not facts, and no patient fact is derived from them.

Supplement Table S1 (DOCX) is an aggregate evidence-level count table by TKI group and holds no patient-level data; it could not be extracted with the text-document tool because anydoc is not installed, so only the manifest row was reviewed from the raw DOCX text.
Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; the four images were inspected separately in the visual submission.

Figure 1 covers 2015 to 2024 while the study window runs to March 2025, which may explain why its bars total 18 rather than 21; the source does not say so, so the difference stays an unexplained limitation.

The Results sentence that 5 patients started immunosuppressive therapy for significant proteinuria and/or renal impairment, guided by immune complex deposition, names no patients; Table 5 shows IS therapy for five patients (Pt 2, 3, 5, 14, 15), but the indication is not assigned to them.
Supplement Table S1 is an aggregate causality evidence-level count table (certain, probable, possible by TKI group); no per-patient values are taken from it.

limitations: Case series of 21 patients; all patient facts come from Tables 1, 3, 4 and 5 and are keyed by the printed Pt number, so patient ids p1 to p21 equal Pt 1 to 21.

Table 4 evidence quotes include the whole patient-number row and analyte row because the cell for one patient is only identifiable by column position; values for other patients appear inside those quotes.
Table 4 caption says 15 patients but 17 patient columns are printed (and the Results text says 17 TMA-like cases); this count mismatch is recorded as arithmetic ambiguity, not a source conflict.
Table 5 prints rows for 18 patients (Pt 17, 20 and 21 are absent) although its caption says 21 patients; no outcome facts are recorded for the absent patients.

Results text says 8 discontinued, 5 substituted and 5 continued the TKI among 18 patients, while Table 5 shows 14 discontinuations and 5 substitutions; arithmetic mismatch kept as ambiguity, no per-patient value changed.

Cohort-level statements (medians, percentages, unlabeled counts such as pre-existing renal comorbidity, schistocyte-negative smears in five cases, prior anti-VEGF antibody exposure in four cases, twelve patients with prior anticancer therapy, one AKI patient, four deaths from cancer progression, causality grades certain and probable) are not assigned to individual patients because the text gives no patient labels.
Table 2 is a group-level summary; only its BTK row (n = 1) is kept, as review_only facts for the sole BTK patient.
Cases 5 and 19 in the causality sentence are matched to Pt 5 and Pt 19 by number only, kept review_only.
Peak U-Pro for Pt 11 differs between Tables 3 and 5 and is kept as two review_only source_conflict facts; TKI duration for Pt 3 and Pt 6 differs only by rounding between Tables 1 and 3.
Table 5 Tumor status has no printed time and is not equated with the Table 1 status at biopsy.

Figure 1 as plotted sums to 18 cases (VEGFR 11, PDGFR 4, HER 2, BTK 1) while the text and tables give 21 patients (VEGFR 12, PDGFR 5, HER 3, BTK 1); plotted values are chart estimates, not facts, and no patient fact is derived from them.

Supplement Table S1 (DOCX) is an aggregate evidence-level count table by TKI group and holds no patient-level data; it could not be extracted with the text-document tool because anydoc is not installed, so only the manifest row was reviewed from the raw DOCX text.
Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; the four images were inspected separately in the visual submission.

Figure 1 covers 2015 to 2024 while the study window runs to March 2025, which may explain why its bars total 18 rather than 21; the source does not say so, so the difference stays an unexplained limitation.

The Results sentence that 5 patients started immunosuppressive therapy for significant proteinuria and/or renal impairment, guided by immune complex deposition, names no patients; Table 5 shows IS therapy for five patients (Pt 2, 3, 5, 14, 15), but the indication is not assigned to them.
Supplement Table S1 is an aggregate causality evidence-level count table (certain, probable, possible by TKI group); no per-patient values are taken from it.

The case series lists this patient as having biopsy-proven TKI-associated renal injury, with edema present and change in hypertension present at the time of renal biopsy. Concomitant medication is not available.

limitations: Case series of 21 patients; all patient facts come from Tables 1, 3, 4 and 5 and are keyed by the printed Pt number, so patient ids p1 to p21 equal Pt 1 to 21.

Table 4 evidence quotes include the whole patient-number row and analyte row because the cell for one patient is only identifiable by column position; values for other patients appear inside those quotes.
Table 4 caption says 15 patients but 17 patient columns are printed (and the Results text says 17 TMA-like cases); this count mismatch is recorded as arithmetic ambiguity, not a source conflict.
Table 5 prints rows for 18 patients (Pt 17, 20 and 21 are absent) although its caption says 21 patients; no outcome facts are recorded for the absent patients.

Results text says 8 discontinued, 5 substituted and 5 continued the TKI among 18 patients, while Table 5 shows 14 discontinuations and 5 substitutions; arithmetic mismatch kept as ambiguity, no per-patient value changed.

Cohort-level statements (medians, percentages, unlabeled counts such as pre-existing renal comorbidity, schistocyte-negative smears in five cases, prior anti-VEGF antibody exposure in four cases, twelve patients with prior anticancer therapy, one AKI patient, four deaths from cancer progression, causality grades certain and probable) are not assigned to individual patients because the text gives no patient labels.
Table 2 is a group-level summary; only its BTK row (n = 1) is kept, as review_only facts for the sole BTK patient.
Cases 5 and 19 in the causality sentence are matched to Pt 5 and Pt 19 by number only, kept review_only.
Peak U-Pro for Pt 11 differs between Tables 3 and 5 and is kept as two review_only source_conflict facts; TKI duration for Pt 3 and Pt 6 differs only by rounding between Tables 1 and 3.
Table 5 Tumor status has no printed time and is not equated with the Table 1 status at biopsy.

Figure 1 as plotted sums to 18 cases (VEGFR 11, PDGFR 4, HER 2, BTK 1) while the text and tables give 21 patients (VEGFR 12, PDGFR 5, HER 3, BTK 1); plotted values are chart estimates, not facts, and no patient fact is derived from them.

Supplement Table S1 (DOCX) is an aggregate evidence-level count table by TKI group and holds no patient-level data; it could not be extracted with the text-document tool because anydoc is not installed, so only the manifest row was reviewed from the raw DOCX text.
Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; the four images were inspected separately in the visual submission.

Figure 1 covers 2015 to 2024 while the study window runs to March 2025, which may explain why its bars total 18 rather than 21; the source does not say so, so the difference stays an unexplained limitation.

The Results sentence that 5 patients started immunosuppressive therapy for significant proteinuria and/or renal impairment, guided by immune complex deposition, names no patients; Table 5 shows IS therapy for five patients (Pt 2, 3, 5, 14, 15), but the indication is not assigned to them.
Supplement Table S1 is an aggregate causality evidence-level count table (certain, probable, possible by TKI group); no per-patient values are taken from it.

claims.text: A male patient aged 49 years with gastrointestinal stromal tumor had received the tyrosine kinase inhibitor Ripretinib for 25 months. The case series lists this patient as having biopsy-proven TKI-associated renal injury, with edema absent and change in hypertension absent at the time of renal biopsy. Concomitant medication is not available.

claims.text: Renal biopsy findings were reported as TMA + FSGS. At the time of renal biopsy, the table gives serum creatinine 1.1 (95) mg/dL (micromole per liter in parentheses), proteinuria 1.41 g/day and serum albumin 38.7 g/L. Nephrotic syndrome is recorded as no, and the creatinine trajectory group is not assessable.

limitations: Case series of 21 patients; all patient facts come from Tables 1, 3, 4 and 5 and are keyed by the printed Pt number, so patient ids p1 to p21 equal Pt 1 to 21.

Table 4 evidence quotes include the whole patient-number row and analyte row because the cell for one patient is only identifiable by column position; values for other patients appear inside those quotes.
Table 4 caption says 15 patients but 17 patient columns are printed (and the Results text says 17 TMA-like cases); this count mismatch is recorded as arithmetic ambiguity, not a source conflict.
Table 5 prints rows for 18 patients (Pt 17, 20 and 21 are absent) although its caption says 21 patients; no outcome facts are recorded for the absent patients.

Results text says 8 discontinued, 5 substituted and 5 continued the TKI among 18 patients, while Table 5 shows 14 discontinuations and 5 substitutions; arithmetic mismatch kept as ambiguity, no per-patient value changed.

Cohort-level statements (medians, percentages, unlabeled counts such as pre-existing renal comorbidity, schistocyte-negative smears in five cases, prior anti-VEGF antibody exposure in four cases, twelve patients with prior anticancer therapy, one AKI patient, four deaths from cancer progression, causality grades certain and probable) are not assigned to individual patients because the text gives no patient labels.
Table 2 is a group-level summary; only its BTK row (n = 1) is kept, as review_only facts for the sole BTK patient.
Cases 5 and 19 in the causality sentence are matched to Pt 5 and Pt 19 by number only, kept review_only.
Peak U-Pro for Pt 11 differs between Tables 3 and 5 and is kept as two review_only source_conflict facts; TKI duration for Pt 3 and Pt 6 differs only by rounding between Tables 1 and 3.
Table 5 Tumor status has no printed time and is not equated with the Table 1 status at biopsy.

Figure 1 as plotted sums to 18 cases (VEGFR 11, PDGFR 4, HER 2, BTK 1) while the text and tables give 21 patients (VEGFR 12, PDGFR 5, HER 3, BTK 1); plotted values are chart estimates, not facts, and no patient fact is derived from them.

Supplement Table S1 (DOCX) is an aggregate evidence-level count table by TKI group and holds no patient-level data; it could not be extracted with the text-document tool because anydoc is not installed, so only the manifest row was reviewed from the raw DOCX text.
Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; the four images were inspected separately in the visual submission.

Figure 1 covers 2015 to 2024 while the study window runs to March 2025, which may explain why its bars total 18 rather than 21; the source does not say so, so the difference stays an unexplained limitation.

The Results sentence that 5 patients started immunosuppressive therapy for significant proteinuria and/or renal impairment, guided by immune complex deposition, names no patients; Table 5 shows IS therapy for five patients (Pt 2, 3, 5, 14, 15), but the indication is not assigned to them.
Supplement Table S1 is an aggregate causality evidence-level count table (certain, probable, possible by TKI group); no per-patient values are taken from it.

claims.text: A male patient aged 58 years with lung cancer had received the tyrosine kinase inhibitor Osimertinib for 14 months. The case series lists this patient as having biopsy-proven TKI-associated renal injury, with edema absent and change in hypertension absent at the time of renal biopsy. Concomitant medication is not available.

claims.text: Renal biopsy findings were reported as CTIN. At the time of renal biopsy, the table gives serum creatinine 1.6 (140) mg/dL (micromole per liter in parentheses), proteinuria 0.41 g/day and serum albumin 54 g/L. Nephrotic syndrome is recorded as no, and the creatinine trajectory group is not assessable.

limitations: Case series of 21 patients; all patient facts come from Tables 1, 3, 4 and 5 and are keyed by the printed Pt number, so patient ids p1 to p21 equal Pt 1 to 21.

Table 4 evidence quotes include the whole patient-number row and analyte row because the cell for one patient is only identifiable by column position; values for other patients appear inside those quotes.
Table 4 caption says 15 patients but 17 patient columns are printed (and the Results text says 17 TMA-like cases); this count mismatch is recorded as arithmetic ambiguity, not a source conflict.
Table 5 prints rows for 18 patients (Pt 17, 20 and 21 are absent) although its caption says 21 patients; no outcome facts are recorded for the absent patients.

Results text says 8 discontinued, 5 substituted and 5 continued the TKI among 18 patients, while Table 5 shows 14 discontinuations and 5 substitutions; arithmetic mismatch kept as ambiguity, no per-patient value changed.

Cohort-level statements (medians, percentages, unlabeled counts such as pre-existing renal comorbidity, schistocyte-negative smears in five cases, prior anti-VEGF antibody exposure in four cases, twelve patients with prior anticancer therapy, one AKI patient, four deaths from cancer progression, causality grades certain and probable) are not assigned to individual patients because the text gives no patient labels.
Table 2 is a group-level summary; only its BTK row (n = 1) is kept, as review_only facts for the sole BTK patient.
Cases 5 and 19 in the causality sentence are matched to Pt 5 and Pt 19 by number only, kept review_only.
Peak U-Pro for Pt 11 differs between Tables 3 and 5 and is kept as two review_only source_conflict facts; TKI duration for Pt 3 and Pt 6 differs only by rounding between Tables 1 and 3.
Table 5 Tumor status has no printed time and is not equated with the Table 1 status at biopsy.

Figure 1 as plotted sums to 18 cases (VEGFR 11, PDGFR 4, HER 2, BTK 1) while the text and tables give 21 patients (VEGFR 12, PDGFR 5, HER 3, BTK 1); plotted values are chart estimates, not facts, and no patient fact is derived from them.

Supplement Table S1 (DOCX) is an aggregate evidence-level count table by TKI group and holds no patient-level data; it could not be extracted with the text-document tool because anydoc is not installed, so only the manifest row was reviewed from the raw DOCX text.
Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; the four images were inspected separately in the visual submission.

Figure 1 covers 2015 to 2024 while the study window runs to March 2025, which may explain why its bars total 18 rather than 21; the source does not say so, so the difference stays an unexplained limitation.

The Results sentence that 5 patients started immunosuppressive therapy for significant proteinuria and/or renal impairment, guided by immune complex deposition, names no patients; Table 5 shows IS therapy for five patients (Pt 2, 3, 5, 14, 15), but the indication is not assigned to them.
Supplement Table S1 is an aggregate causality evidence-level count table (certain, probable, possible by TKI group); no per-patient values are taken from it.
